messages:
Alex (eng-platform): quick follow-up from the canary fallback RFC — thinking about traffic 'leases' as the ownership primitive for short-lived canary routing. want to sketch tradeoffs and a small API so router/controller responsibilities are explicit.
Riya (eng-runtime): +1. curious how you see leases interacting with autoscaling and session affinity.
Alex (eng-platform): good point. idea is: controller grants a lease token for a traffic segment for N seconds. router uses token to route traffic to canary pool. token expiry = automatic drift back to baseline if controller disappears. keeps fallback simple.
Sam (eng-sre): does expiry mean instant cutover? we need graceful drain windows otherwise we risk interrupting in-flight requests.
Alex (eng-platform): not instant — lease has states. propose: PENDING -> ACTIVE -> DRAINING -> EXPIRED. router honors DRAINING by stopping new sessions but finishing in-flight. small drain TTL on router side (default 30s).
Taylor (eng-infra): how do we persist tokens? in-memory on controller would be lowest latency, but we need cross-zone resilience. recommend a lightweight, strongly-consistent lease store (etcd/consul) with short TTL and leader pinning.
Riya (eng-runtime): runtime needs an offline mode if lease store is slow — fallback to local cached token with conservative expiry to avoid split-brain. we should keep controller health heartbeat tied to lease refresh rate.
Jordan (product): for enterprise tenants, can we scope leases per-customer so a tenant rollback doesn't affect global traffic? customers care about isolation.
Alex (eng-platform): yes — lease is namespaced: {cluster, model, tenant, segment}. controller policy decides granularity. we also add a policy flag for global vs tenant-scoped fallback.
Sam (eng-sre): telemetry — we must emit lease_acquired, lease_refreshed, lease_released, lease_failed and include metrics for race conditions where two controllers try to acquire same segment.
Alex (eng-platform): agreed. also add fast-probe hooks: router can run health probe simulations through the canary pool before counting it live. probe failures should reduce effective lease capacity but not immediately expire token.
Riya (eng-runtime): small API sketch — keeping it intentionally tiny:
```
// controller -> lease store
Lease Acquire(ctx, segment_id, duration_s) -> {token, expires_at, owner_id}
Lease Refresh(ctx, token, extend_s) -> {token, expires_at}
Lease Release(ctx, token)
Lease Observe(ctx, segment_id) -> {owner_id, state, expires_at}
```
Router behaviour: attach `x-canary-lease: <token>` header to routed requests and honor DRAINING semantics locally.
Taylor (eng-infra): if lease store is etcd, we can rely on TTL-based keys and watcher streams for routers to subscribe. downside: etcd watch scale at ~10k watchers is rough; maybe we make a fanout service (lease-proxy) that consolidates watchers.
Sam (eng-sre): rollout safety: controller should be able to request 'soft-quota' on a lease (e.g., max_rps or fraction) so router can throttle before full cutover. this reduces blast radius.
Alex (eng-platform): yes — include optional constraints: {max_rps, max_sessions, weight}. controller uses probing + constraints to grow weight.
Jordan (product): customers will want predictable failover SLAs. can we document typical timings: acquisition ~100-300ms, refresh every 5s, expiry 15s -> total safety window?
Riya (eng-runtime): those numbers feel right as defaults. make them config per-deployment. also note cost: very short refresh intervals increase control plane load. need adaptive refresh (longer for stable canaries).
Taylor (eng-infra): implementation note: avoid persisting large token blobs. token should be compact (uuid + HMAC) so routers can validate locally if we want offline allowance. key rotation for HMAC must be in the flow.
Sam (eng-sre): incident case: controller crash and slow lease expiry caused double-serving in two data centers. mitigation: prefer conservative default expiry + explicit revoke path where a new leader can mark old owner revoked and signal routers.
Alex (eng-platform): agree. add RevokeLease(token) and OwnerChange event with revocation reason. routers must treat OwnerChange as immediate trigger to re-evaluate routing.
deploy-bot: deploy noted: canary-lease-proto v0.1 pushed to staging at 2026-03-20T09:12:03Z :rocket:
Riya (eng-runtime): next steps: I'll prototype router side semantics (token validation, draining) this week. Alex — can you write a short RFC appendix with the API + expected latencies and failure modes?
Alex (eng-platform): will do. I'll include test cases for split-brain, probe flapping, and lease-proxy scaling. thanks all. :thumbsup:
